title: Auth flows — golden recording request

config_instances.default: config template from reports/oracle/BOOTSTRAP.md §3 (as above). Client IP = docker bridge gateway (a REMOTE client; allow-remote: true).
config_instances.open: same as default but api-keys removed entirely (open-proxy instance)
config_instances.safemode: same as default but api-keys: ["your-api-key-1"] (template-value instance)
config_instances.no-mgmt-secret: same as default but the whole remote-management block removed
config_instances.mgmt-local-only: same as default but remote-management.allow-remote: false
config_instances.fresh-ban: same as default, started FRESH immediately before the ban cases (per-IP failure counter must start at 0)

secrets_note: Request headers below use <api-key> = oracle-local-key-1 and <mgmt-key> = oracle-mgmt-key-1 from your config template; do not copy other secrets. <port> = 18317.
mock_upstream: None needed for S3: no provider credentials are in scope. The reference binary itself on 127.0.0.1:18317 is the target. mock-upstream mode flags (happy/upstream-error/slow-chunks/disconnect-mid-stream) do not apply to S3 cases.
ordering_constraints: Cases 19-20 (IP ban) MUST run in the fresh-ban instance, in that order (reset case first, ban case last); the ban poisons the client IP for 30 minutes.
In the default instance, run all other cases first; the missing-key/invalid-key cases each add one failure to the per-IP counter (2 total) but never reach the threshold of 5.
Multi-request cases (33-34) must run their steps in the listed order; the state from step 1 is captured and substituted in later steps (record the substitution in meta.yaml).
auth-url cases leave a 5-minute background waiter per state; harmless, do not wait for it.
record_format: Per case directory tests/fixtures/S3/<case-id>/: meta.yaml, request.http (or one request per step, suffixed), downstream.md per step, upstream.jsonl NOT needed (no mock upstream; omit or leave empty with a note), mock-response.json not needed.
dynamic_fields_common: Content-Length (mask only if body bytes recorded)
X-Cpa-Trace-Id/X-Request-Id style trace headers if present

cases.purpose: No credential anywhere on a proxied route -> 401 {"error":"Missing API key"} (auth error string shape, S3 §2.1).
cases.record: status + response headers + exact body bytes

cases.purpose: Credential present (Bearer) but not in the key set -> 401 {"error":"Invalid API key"}.
Valid Bearer key accepted on /v1 (no providers configured -> empty model list).
Authorization header WITHOUT Bearer prefix: entire header value is compared as the key (extractBearerToken quirk, S3 §2.1).
X-Goog-Api-Key accepted on /v1beta (Gemini-style key source).
X-Api-Key (Anthropic-style) accepted as key source on /v1.
Query parameter key=<key> accepted (S3 §2.1 source 4).
Query parameter auth_token=<key> accepted (S3 §2.1 source 5).
api-keys unconfigured -> NO auth provider -> request allowed without any credential (open proxy, S3 §2.1 + O-2).
Template api-key safe mode: proxied route 403 with X-CPA-SAFE-MODE header and unsafe_example_api_key body; root serves the warning HTML instead of the normal payload (S3 §2.1).
cases.record: status + headers + body for both steps

cases.purpose: Realtime route without auth -> 401 with OpenAI-shaped error {message,type:authentication_error,param:null,code:invalid_api_key} (S3 §2.1 realtime branch).
Realtime route with a wrong Bearer key -> 401 invalid_api_key realtime shape.
Management route without any key -> 401 {"error":"missing management key"} (failure counted).
Management route with wrong X-Management-Key -> 401 {"error":"invalid management key"} (failure counted).
Valid X-Management-Key accepted (bcrypt compare of plaintext vs stored hash).
Authorization: Bearer <mgmt-key> accepted on a management route (S3 §2.2 key extraction).
allow-remote: false + request from a REMOTE client (docker gateway) -> 403 {"error":"remote management disabled"} even with the valid key (gate runs before key validation; no failure counted).
No remote-management secret at all -> management routes never registered -> 404 EMPTY body (R-404) even with a key header.
Sliding counter resets on success: 4 invalid keys (4x401), then valid key (200), then 4 invalid keys again (4x401) — never banned.
cases.record: status + headers + body for every request (12 responses)
cases.notes: Run BEFORE s3-mgmt-ban-after-5-invalid in the same fresh instance. Record every response; the contract asserts the 200 in the middle and 401s around it.

cases.purpose: 5 counted failures -> IP banned: 6th request (even with a VALID key) -> 403 {"error":"IP banned due to too many failed attempts. Try again in <duration>"} (S3 §2.2).
cases.record: status + headers + body for every request (6 responses)
dynamic_fields: ban countdown duration in body (mask; format is Go duration string like 29m59s)
cases.notes: Run LAST in the fresh-ban instance (after the reset case). The final 403 body's countdown is dynamic — mask the duration token, keep the surrounding text exact.

cases.purpose: GET /anthropic/callback with a state that matches no pending session: callback write is silently skipped, response is STILL 200 success HTML (S3 §2.4 / O-3).
cases.record: status + headers + exact HTML body bytes

cases.purpose: Same 200-HTML-always contract for /codex/callback with an error param present (error is written into the skipped callback file; response still 200 HTML).
cases.record: status + headers + exact HTML body bytes

cases.purpose: Devin callback is strict: GET /devin/callback with neither code nor error -> 400 {"error":"code or error is required"}.
Devin callback with a code but no matching pending session -> 400 {"error":"invalid or expired OAuth callback"}.
POST /v0/management/oauth-callback with unparseable JSON -> 400 {"status":"error","error":"invalid body"} (no management key needed on this route).
POST with parseable body but no state -> 400 "state is required".
POST with state containing invalid characters (space) -> 400 "invalid state" (state regex [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1..128}).
Valid-syntax state but neither code nor error -> 400 "code or error is required" (checked before session lookup).
Valid-syntax state that was never registered -> 404 {"status":"error","error":"unknown or expired state"}.

GET /v0/management/anthropic-auth-url -> 200 {"state","status","url"}: url = https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize with the exact query parameter set (code=true, client_id, code_challenge, code_challenge_method=S256, redirect_uri=http://localhost:54545/callback, response_type=code, scope, state). Records exact byte order of the JSON map serialization.
cases.record: status + headers + body. Mask: state value (32-hex) and the url's state/code_challenge parameter values; keep parameter NAMES, order, and all other values exact.
cases.notes: No vendor network call happens on this path; a 5-minute background waiter polls for a callback file — do not wait for it. Do not send is_webui.

cases.purpose: GET /v0/management/codex-auth-url -> 200 with https://auth.openai.com/oauth/authorize URL incl. prompt=login, id_token_add_organizations=true, codex_cli_simplified_flow=true, scope=openid email profile offline_access, redirect_uri=http://localhost:1455/auth/callback (S3 §2.3.2).
cases.record: status + headers + body (mask state + code_challenge values)

cases.purpose: GET /v0/management/antigravity-auth-url -> 200 with https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth URL incl. access_type=offline, prompt=consent, redirect_uri=http://localhost:51121/oauth-callback, 5 googleapis scopes (S3 §2.3.3).

GET /v0/management/devin-auth-url -> 200 with https://app.devin.ai/auth/cli/continue URL; query order: redirect_uri=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback, state, prompt=select_account, code_challenge, code_challenge_method=S256 (NOT alphabetical; hand-built order, S3 §2.3.4).
cases.record: status + headers + body (mask state + code_challenge values; <port> = 18317)

cases.purpose: Full pending-session lifecycle with no vendor network: anthropic-auth-url registers state S -> get-auth-status?state=S = wait -> DELETE oauth-session?state=S = {cancelled:true} -> get-auth-status = unknown or expired state -> oauth-callback POST with S = 404 unknown or expired state (S3 §2.5).
cases.record: status + headers + body for all 5 steps; record $S substitution in meta.yaml
cases.notes: Expected: step2 {"status":"wait"}; step3 {"status":"ok","cancelled":true}; step4 {"status":"error","error":"unknown or expired state"}; step5 404 {"status":"error","error":"unknown or expired state"}. JSON key order per recording.

cases.purpose: codex-auth-url registers state S as a codex session; POST oauth-callback with provider=anthropic + S + code -> 400 {"status":"error","error":"provider does not match state"} (S3 §2.4 ladder step 9).
cases.record: status + headers + body for both steps
cases.notes: Step 2 does NOT hit any vendor endpoint: the mismatch check fires before the callback file is written.

cases.purpose: GET /v0/management/get-auth-status without state param -> 200 {"status":"ok"}.
GET /v0/management/get-auth-status?state=<invalid> -> 400 {"status":"error","error":"invalid state"}.
DELETE /v0/management/oauth-session without state -> 400 {"status":"error","error":"missing state"}.
